newsitem.title: USA: RENAULT NOT PLANNING N.A. RETURN.
newsitem.headline: RENAULT NOT PLANNING N.A. RETURN.

text.p: French car maker Renault Group has no plans to return to the North American market, although a top company executive said an automaker needs to be in this market to be considered a global competitor.

Renault Executive Vice President Carlos Ghosn also said that given the success Chrysler Corp has had with the Jeep vehicle brands, Renault would not repeat its 1987 sale of American Motors Corp to Chrysler.
Ghosn's comments came earlier this week at the University of Michigan's annual auto conference.

In prepared remarks, Ghosn said Renault is pursuing a strategy of international expansion in South America, Asia and Russia to lessen its dependence on Western Europe, which accounts for 80 percent of Renault's sales.
Renault is initially focusing on South America. It expects to start production in December 1998 at a new passenger car plant in Brazil. The facility will have capacity to make 250,000 cars a year.
The company has also launched cost-cutting programs with a goal of reducing supply costs by $2 billion before 2000.

Renault is the ninth-largest car maker in the world, Ghosn said, producing 1.8 million passenger cars in 1996. The company was owned by the French government until 1991. In July last year, private investment in the firm reached 54 percent.
